claims.text: Factored Verification achieves 76.2% accuracy on hallucination detection in the summarization task of the HaluEval benchmark.
ChatGPT (16k) averages 0.62 hallucinations per summary when summarizing across multiple academic papers.
GPT-4 averages 0.84 hallucinations per summary when summarizing across multiple academic papers.
Claude 2 averages 1.55 hallucinations per summary when summarizing across multiple academic papers.
Self-correction using factored critiques reduces average hallucinations per summary to 0.49 for ChatGPT.
Self-correction using factored critiques reduces average hallucinations per summary to 0.46 for GPT-4.
Self-correction using factored critiques reduces average hallucinations per summary to 0.95 for Claude 2.

evidence.description: Factored Verification sets a new SotA on hallucination detection in the summarization task of the HaluEval benchmark, achieving 76.2% accuracy.
Measured 0.62 hallucinations in the average ChatGPT (16k) summary when summarizing across multiple academic papers.
Measured 0.84 hallucinations in the average GPT-4 summary when summarizing across multiple academic papers.
Measured 1.55 hallucinations in the average Claude 2 summary when summarizing across multiple academic papers.
Asking models to self-correct using factored critiques lowers the number of hallucinations to 0.49 for ChatGPT.
Asking models to self-correct using factored critiques lowers the number of hallucinations to 0.46 for GPT-4.
Asking models to self-correct using factored critiques lowers the number of hallucinations to 0.95 for Claude 2.

methodologies.name: Factored Verification
methodologies.description: An automated method for detecting hallucinations in abstractive summaries and leveraging factored critiques for model self-correction.

limitations.text: Hallucinations produced when summarizing academic papers are often subtle and difficult to detect.
